## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

1	# Spec: Codec export C6b — 4K on every export row, the idle three-run speeds, the final time constants
2	
3	## Goal
4	Measure, on an idle machine, every video export row at 4K and each bundled-encoder key three times at 1080p and 4K on real camera footage, and use the medians to replace `ExportEncoderCosts`' provisional time constants (and raise memory figures the new peaks exceed). Record it all as a CX-18 amendment, a `## C6b` road-map record, and the guide's and proof README's sentences, with the estimate checked against an export it was not fitted on.
5	
6	## Files
7	All paths are in the worktree `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`, at cbf6e83).
8	- `tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`: new keys, `--media/--fps/--seconds/--from/--runs/--label/--derive`, the per-run frame count, `estimated_seconds` capture, `uptime` in the JSON, outputs deleted after reading.
9	- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift`: the `time` table's constants (and `setupSeconds`), `memory` figures the max rule raises, the `run` source strings, and the doc comments with "provisional" removed.
10	- `tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py`: P0 requires each time source to carry `C6b` and no `provisional` (line 322), plus the docstring's P0 line.
11	- `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`: an "**Amended by C6b**" paragraph under CX-18. It supersedes (9)'s PROVISIONAL and the closing risk's "single-run figure", and holds the figures. CX-13 and CX-16 carry no provisional mark (checked: `grep -n provisional` hits only CX-18), so they are left as they are.
12	- `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md`: the CX-18 row and the `codec-export.md` row lose "provisional" and name C6b. The `codec-export.md` Lines cell is updated.
13	- `designs/spec/07.8-export.md`: line ~337, "provisional single-run figures until C6b", becomes the C6b medians sentence.
14	- `designs/spec/README.md`: the `07.8-export.md` Lines cell and the `11-decisions/` folder cell (`N in 33 files`).
15	- `designs/codec-export.md`: a `## C6b — 4K on every row and the final time constants` section with `### Record`, appended after C6a's "Fix pass 1" (end of file).
16	- `docs/guide/export.md`: line 34's "one measured export per format", the Speed table's rows 89–91 (the measured time and size relative to Balanced), line 206's GB ranges if `memory` changes, and line 336's provisional limit.
17	- `tools/proof/README.md`: the C6a section's `encoder_memory_measure.py` paragraph (line ~25413) gains the new flags, the GH5 fixture and where it comes from, and the four C6b batch commands.
18	
19	## Interfaces
20	`encoder_memory_measure.py` CLI (the defaults reproduce C6a's run exactly):
21	```
22	python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py [--app debug|release|<.app>] [--only K1,K2]
23	    [--sizes 1080,1440,2160] [--media av|gh5|<path>] [--fps 30] [--seconds 10] [--from 0]
24	    [--runs 1] [--label memory]

26	```
27	- `SIZES` adds `"1440": (2560, 1440)`.
28	- `KEYS` values become `(preset, speed, hlg, sized)`. The new keys are `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `gif`, `apng`, with `sized=True` on `gif` and `apng` only. A sized key's `export` passes `size: [w, h]`, because their default is the format's cap. `EXTENSIONS` adds `hevc mp4, hevc_alpha mov, hevc_10bit mp4, prores_422 mov, prores_4444 mov, gif gif, apng apng`.
29	- `GH5 = HERE / "media" / "log-samples" / "panasonic_lumix_gh5_sample_movie__borough_market___4k_uhd___25p___10_bit___800_iso___v_log_l_photo_style_v1 (2160p).mp4"`. This is H.264 High 8-bit 3840×2160 25p, 55.21 s, gitignored owner media, and the spike's `gh5` source.
30	- `--media av`: C6a's layout, AV.mov at 0 and 5 s, no range. It is refused with any `--seconds` other than 10 or `--from` other than 0. Any other media goes once at 0, then `set_range(start=from·SEC, end=(from+seconds)·SEC)`, and `export` gets `range: "in_out"`.
31	- Row keys add `run`, `expected_frames`, `estimated_seconds` (from one `export_status` call right after `export`, then `client.wait_export(id, seconds=EXPORT_BOUND)`), `fps`, `media`, `from`, `seconds_range`. The frame counts are computed as follows:
32	  - `written_frames` = done `duration` × the done settings' `fps` num ÷ (den × SEC).
33	  - `expected_frames` = round(`seconds` × that fps).
34	  - A difference of more than 1 frame is the row's `error`.
35	  - `per_frame_seconds` = `elapsed / written_frames`.

38	- `--derive LONG SHORT` launches nothing. It prints, per writer key, the following:

47	0. **Up-front machine-time estimate.** All batches are at 25 fps. B and S cover 7 keys: `av1:faster`, `av1:balanced`, `av1:smaller`, `av1_webm:balanced`, `vp9_webm:sdr`, `vp9_webm:hlg`, `vp9_alpha_webm`. Each run has about 10 s of overhead (launch, 152 MB import, warm frame). The fps on the GH5 are the spike's real-content 10-bit rates, with 4K at ¼ of them. "Worst" means double the encode time, and GIF/APNG at their 900 s bound.

52	   | A | 4K, 1 run: h264, hevc, hevc_alpha, hevc_10bit, prores_422, prores_4444, gif (125 fr), apng (250 fr) | 8 | 6 min | 32 min |
53	   | B | 7 keys × 1080, 2160 × 3 runs, 10 s (250 frames) | 42 | 19 min | 31 min |

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

cbf6e83 Codec export C5 (#377, spec §11 CX-17): VP9 with alpha in WebM
     228 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py
     206 app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift
     617 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py
    1051 total
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18): what one bundled-encoder export costs — its resident
peak above the instance's own, and its wall time — measured over MCP, per Export Queue key,
at 1080p and 4K. `ExportEncoderCosts.swift`'s two tables are transcribed from its table,
and `designs/codec-export.md`'s "## C6a" records the run.

Every run is one fresh instance of the app `proof_app` chooses (`RC_PROOF_APP`, Release for
the record), on a scratch socket, stopped by its own PID; nothing else is ever killed. Each:

  new_project; set_canvas <w>×<h> at 30 fps (output hlg for the HLG key); AV.mov imported
  and placed twice on the first track (0 and 5 s: 10 s, 300 frames); one render_frame to
  warm the compositor; the baseline `ps -o rss= -p <pid>`; then `export` (the key's preset,
  and encoder_speed on the AV1 rows) followed to `done` while a thread samples the RSS every
  0.1 s. delta = peak − baseline; seconds = the done answer's `elapsed`; the 1-minute load
  average is read at the export's start.

Keys: av1 and av1_webm at faster, balanced and smaller; vp9_webm in an SDR project and in
an HLG one; vp9_alpha_webm (codec-export C5, always 8-bit SDR) in an SDR project; h264 as the
AVFoundation control. Sizes 1920×1080 and 3840×2160.

  python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py [--app debug|release|<.app>]
                                                [--only av1:balanced,h264] [--sizes 1080,2160]

Writes `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/<date>/memory.json` and prints the table. A run
that fails is a row with its error, never an exit; the script exits 1 when any run failed.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402

AV = HERE / "media" / "AV.mov"
SEC = 600_000
FRAMES = 300
SIZES = {"1080": (1920, 1080), "2160": (3840, 2160)}
# name → (preset, encoder_speed or None, HLG project)
KEYS = {
    "av1:faster": ("av1", "faster", False),
    "av1:balanced": ("av1", "balanced", False),
    "av1:smaller": ("av1", "smaller", False),
    "av1_webm:faster": ("av1_webm", "faster", False),
    "av1_webm:balanced": ("av1_webm", "balanced", False),
    "av1_webm:smaller": ("av1_webm", "smaller", False),
    "vp9_webm:sdr": ("vp9_webm", None, False),
    "vp9_webm:hlg": ("vp9_webm", None, True),
    "vp9_alpha_webm": ("vp9_alpha_webm", None, False),
    "h264": ("h264", None, False),
}
EXTENSIONS = {"av1": "mp4", "av1_webm": "webm", "vp9_webm": "webm", "vp9_alpha_webm": "webm",
              "h264": "mp4"}
SAMPLE_EVERY = 0.1
EXPORT_BOUND = 900


def rss_bytes(pid):
    """The process's resident size in bytes, or None once it is gone."""
    got = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    text = got.stdout.strip()
    return int(text) * 1024 if text.isdigit() else None


class Sampler(threading.Thread):
    """Samples one PID's RSS every `SAMPLE_EVERY` s until stopped; keeps the peak."""

    def __init__(self, pid):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.pid, self.peak, self.samples = pid, 0, 0
        self.halt = threading.Event()

    def run(self):
        while not self.halt.is_set():
            value = rss_bytes(self.pid)
            if value is not None:
                self.peak = max(self.peak, value)
                self.samples += 1
            self.halt.wait(SAMPLE_EVERY)


def measure(app, work, key, size):
    preset, speed, hlg = KEYS[key]
    width, height = SIZES[size]
    label = f"{key.replace(':', '-')}-{size}"
    folder = work / label
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    row = {"key": key, "preset": preset, "encoder_speed": speed, "hlg": hlg,
           "width": width, "height": height, "frames": FRAMES}
    launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), [], env=bounded.child_env({}),
                          log_path=str(folder / "instance.log"), timeout=EXPORT_BOUND + 60)
    try:
        client = launched.client
        if client is None:
            row["error"] = f"the app did not listen ({folder / 'instance.log'})"
            return row
        pid = launched.child.pid
        doc = str(folder / f"{label}.framejob")
        client.call("new_project", path=doc)

        def call(tool, **arguments):
            return client.call_with(tool, {"project": doc, **arguments})
        canvas = {"width": width, "height": height, "fps": 30}
        if hlg:
            canvas["output"] = "hlg"
        try:
            call("set_canvas", **canvas)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):
                raise
        media = call("import_media", path=str(AV))["media"]
        track = call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=0)
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=5 * SEC)
        call("render_frame", t=2 * SEC, path=str(folder / "warm.png"))
        time.sleep(1.0)
        baseline = rss_bytes(pid)
        if baseline is None:
            # Subtracting 0 would record the whole peak as the job's delta: a failed case,
            # never a figure for the cost table.
            row["error"] = f"the baseline RSS of pid {pid} could not be read"
            return row
        out = folder / f"out.{EXTENSIONS[preset]}"
        out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        arguments = {"project": doc, "path": str(out), "preset": preset}
        if speed:
            arguments["encoder_speed"] = speed
        row["load_1min"] = round(os.getloadavg()[0], 2)
        sampler = Sampler(pid)
        sampler.start()
        try:
            done = client.export_with(arguments, seconds=EXPORT_BOUND)
        finally:
            sampler.halt.set()
            sampler.join()
        frames = (done.get("duration", 0) * 30) // SEC if isinstance(done, dict) else None
        row.update({
            "baseline_bytes": baseline, "peak_bytes": sampler.peak,
            "delta_bytes": sampler.peak - baseline, "samples": sampler.samples,
            "seconds": done.get("elapsed"), "bytes": done.get("bytes"),
            "written_frames": frames,
            "per_frame_seconds": round(done.get("elapsed", 0) / FRAMES, 5)})
        call("close_project", discard=True)
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, OSError, proof_app.StaleApp) as error:
        row["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:
        launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)
        try:
            complaints = [line.strip() for line in
                          (folder / "instance.log").read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
                          if "Frame Job: " in line]
        except OSError:
            complaints = ["the log could not be read"]
        row["log_complaints"] = complaints
    return row


def gib(value):
    return f"{value / 1_073_741_824:.2f}" if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else "—"


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="encoder memory and time (codec-export C6a)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated keys, of " + ", ".join(KEYS))
    parser.add_argument("--sizes", default="1080,2160", help="comma-separated, of 1080,2160")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    keys = args.only.split(",") if args.only else list(KEYS)
    sizes = args.sizes.split(",")
    unknown = [k for k in keys if k not in KEYS] + [s for s in sizes if s not in SIZES]
    if unknown:
        print(f"unknown keys or sizes: {unknown}")
        return 2
    try:
        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        return 1
    work = HERE / "work" / "encoder-memory" / date.today().isoformat()
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    physical = int(subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.memsize"], capture_output=True,
                                  text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    machine = subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"], capture_output=True,
                             text=True).stdout.strip()
    print(f"app {app}\nmachine {machine}, {physical / 1_073_741_824:.0f} GiB", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for size in sizes:
        for key in keys:
            row = measure(app, work, key, size)
            rows.append(row)
            print(f"  {key:18} {size}: " + (row["error"] if "error" in row else
                  f"Δ {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} GiB (base {gib(row['baseline_bytes'])}, peak "
                  f"{gib(row['peak_bytes'])}), {row['seconds']} s, load {row['load_1min']}"),
                  flush=True)
            (work / "memory.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                {"app": str(app), "machine": machine, "physical_bytes": physical,
                 "date": date.today().isoformat(), "rows": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(f"\n| Key | Size | Δ RSS GiB | Baseline GiB | Peak GiB | Seconds | s/frame | Load |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for row in rows:
        if "error" in row:
            print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {row['error']} |")
            continue
        print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} | "

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18): what one bundled-encoder export costs — its resident
peak above the instance's own, and its wall time — measured over MCP, per Export Queue key,
at 1080p and 4K. `ExportEncoderCosts.swift`'s two tables are transcribed from its table,
and `designs/codec-export.md`'s "## C6a" records the run.

Every run is one fresh instance of the app `proof_app` chooses (`RC_PROOF_APP`, Release for
the record), on a scratch socket, stopped by its own PID; nothing else is ever killed. Each:

  new_project; set_canvas <w>×<h> at 30 fps (output hlg for the HLG key); AV.mov imported
  and placed twice on the first track (0 and 5 s: 10 s, 300 frames); one render_frame to
  warm the compositor; the baseline `ps -o rss= -p <pid>`; then `export` (the key's preset,
  and encoder_speed on the AV1 rows) followed to `done` while a thread samples the RSS every
  0.1 s. delta = peak − baseline; seconds = the done answer's `elapsed`; the 1-minute load
  average is read at the export's start.

Keys: av1 and av1_webm at faster, balanced and smaller; vp9_webm in an SDR project and in
an HLG one; vp9_alpha_webm (codec-export C5, always 8-bit SDR) in an SDR project; h264 as the
AVFoundation control. Sizes 1920×1080 and 3840×2160.

  python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py [--app debug|release|<.app>]
                                                [--only av1:balanced,h264] [--sizes 1080,2160]

Writes `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/<date>/memory.json` and prints the table. A run
that fails is a row with its error, never an exit; the script exits 1 when any run failed.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402

AV = HERE / "media" / "AV.mov"
SEC = 600_000
FRAMES = 300
SIZES = {"1080": (1920, 1080), "2160": (3840, 2160)}
# name → (preset, encoder_speed or None, HLG project)
KEYS = {
    "av1:faster": ("av1", "faster", False),
    "av1:balanced": ("av1", "balanced", False),
    "av1:smaller": ("av1", "smaller", False),
    "av1_webm:faster": ("av1_webm", "faster", False),
    "av1_webm:balanced": ("av1_webm", "balanced", False),
    "av1_webm:smaller": ("av1_webm", "smaller", False),
    "vp9_webm:sdr": ("vp9_webm", None, False),
    "vp9_webm:hlg": ("vp9_webm", None, True),
    "vp9_alpha_webm": ("vp9_alpha_webm", None, False),
    "h264": ("h264", None, False),
}
EXTENSIONS = {"av1": "mp4", "av1_webm": "webm", "vp9_webm": "webm", "vp9_alpha_webm": "webm",
              "h264": "mp4"}
SAMPLE_EVERY = 0.1
EXPORT_BOUND = 900


def rss_bytes(pid):
    """The process's resident size in bytes, or None once it is gone."""
    got = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    text = got.stdout.strip()
    return int(text) * 1024 if text.isdigit() else None


class Sampler(threading.Thread):
    """Samples one PID's RSS every `SAMPLE_EVERY` s until stopped; keeps the peak."""

    def __init__(self, pid):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.pid, self.peak, self.samples = pid, 0, 0
        self.halt = threading.Event()

    def run(self):
        while not self.halt.is_set():
            value = rss_bytes(self.pid)
            if value is not None:
                self.peak = max(self.peak, value)
                self.samples += 1
            self.halt.wait(SAMPLE_EVERY)


def measure(app, work, key, size):
    preset, speed, hlg = KEYS[key]
    width, height = SIZES[size]
    label = f"{key.replace(':', '-')}-{size}"
    folder = work / label
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    row = {"key": key, "preset": preset, "encoder_speed": speed, "hlg": hlg,
           "width": width, "height": height, "frames": FRAMES}
    launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), [], env=bounded.child_env({}),
                          log_path=str(folder / "instance.log"), timeout=EXPORT_BOUND + 60)
    try:
        client = launched.client
        if client is None:
            row["error"] = f"the app did not listen ({folder / 'instance.log'})"
            return row
        pid = launched.child.pid
        doc = str(folder / f"{label}.framejob")
        client.call("new_project", path=doc)

        def call(tool, **arguments):
            return client.call_with(tool, {"project": doc, **arguments})
        canvas = {"width": width, "height": height, "fps": 30}
        if hlg:
            canvas["output"] = "hlg"
        try:
            call("set_canvas", **canvas)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):
                raise
        media = call("import_media", path=str(AV))["media"]
        track = call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=0)
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=5 * SEC)
        call("render_frame", t=2 * SEC, path=str(folder / "warm.png"))
        time.sleep(1.0)
        baseline = rss_bytes(pid)
        if baseline is None:
            # Subtracting 0 would record the whole peak as the job's delta: a failed case,
            # never a figure for the cost table.
            row["error"] = f"the baseline RSS of pid {pid} could not be read"
            return row
        out = folder / f"out.{EXTENSIONS[preset]}"
        out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        arguments = {"project": doc, "path": str(out), "preset": preset}
        if speed:
            arguments["encoder_speed"] = speed
        row["load_1min"] = round(os.getloadavg()[0], 2)
        sampler = Sampler(pid)
        sampler.start()
        try:
            done = client.export_with(arguments, seconds=EXPORT_BOUND)
        finally:
            sampler.halt.set()
            sampler.join()
        frames = (done.get("duration", 0) * 30) // SEC if isinstance(done, dict) else None
        row.update({
            "baseline_bytes": baseline, "peak_bytes": sampler.peak,
            "delta_bytes": sampler.peak - baseline, "samples": sampler.samples,
            "seconds": done.get("elapsed"), "bytes": done.get("bytes"),
            "written_frames": frames,
            "per_frame_seconds": round(done.get("elapsed", 0) / FRAMES, 5)})
        call("close_project", discard=True)
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, OSError, proof_app.StaleApp) as error:
        row["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:
        launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)
        try:
            complaints = [line.strip() for line in
                          (folder / "instance.log").read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
                          if "Frame Job: " in line]
        except OSError:
            complaints = ["the log could not be read"]
        row["log_complaints"] = complaints
    return row


def gib(value):
    return f"{value / 1_073_741_824:.2f}" if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else "—"


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="encoder memory and time (codec-export C6a)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated keys, of " + ", ".join(KEYS))
    parser.add_argument("--sizes", default="1080,2160", help="comma-separated, of 1080,2160")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    keys = args.only.split(",") if args.only else list(KEYS)
    sizes = args.sizes.split(",")
    unknown = [k for k in keys if k not in KEYS] + [s for s in sizes if s not in SIZES]
    if unknown:
        print(f"unknown keys or sizes: {unknown}")
        return 2
    try:
        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        return 1
    work = HERE / "work" / "encoder-memory" / date.today().isoformat()
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    physical = int(subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.memsize"], capture_output=True,
                                  text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    machine = subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"], capture_output=True,
                             text=True).stdout.strip()
    print(f"app {app}\nmachine {machine}, {physical / 1_073_741_824:.0f} GiB", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for size in sizes:
        for key in keys:
            row = measure(app, work, key, size)
            rows.append(row)
            print(f"  {key:18} {size}: " + (row["error"] if "error" in row else
                  f"Δ {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} GiB (base {gib(row['baseline_bytes'])}, peak "
                  f"{gib(row['peak_bytes'])}), {row['seconds']} s, load {row['load_1min']}"),
                  flush=True)
            (work / "memory.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                {"app": str(app), "machine": machine, "physical_bytes": physical,
                 "date": date.today().isoformat(), "rows": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(f"\n| Key | Size | Δ RSS GiB | Baseline GiB | Peak GiB | Seconds | s/frame | Load |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for row in rows:
        if "error" in row:
            print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {row['error']} |")
            continue
        print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} | "
              f"{gib(row['baseline_bytes'])} | {gib(row['peak_bytes'])} | {row['seconds']} | "
              f"{row['per_frame_seconds']} | {row['load_1min']} |")
    print(f"\n{work / 'memory.json'}")
    failed = [r for r in rows if "error" in r or r.get("log_complaints")]
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18): the Export Queue's memory limit on bundled-encoder
jobs, the held job's sentence, `export_status`'s `waiting` and `estimated_seconds`, and the
export sheet's time estimate.

The probe rows run `encoder_limit_probe.swift`, built through `swift_build.build()` over
`app/Sources` with `Blank.mp4`, `Fonts` and a `default.metallib` of `Compositor.metal` and
`ExportI010.metal` beside it, into `tools/proof/work/encoder-limit/probe/` (reused when
every input is byte-identical). It needs no app and no instance: its two live projects —
A1 (`av1_export_proof.av_doc`'s: 640 × 360, AV.mov from 0 under a two-second text clip) and
W9 (`webm_export_proof.long_doc`'s: 1920 × 1080, AV.mov 24 times at scale 3) — are built in
the probe from AV.mov, as `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's. Every expected value is
computed HERE from P0's dump of the tables, in this file's own arithmetic.

  B0  the probe builds and answers (a probe that does not build is B0's FAIL, and every
      probe row's)
  P0  both tables dumped: the nine keys (av1, av1_webm × faster/balanced/smaller at 10
      bits; vp9_webm at 8 and 10; vp9_alpha_webm at 8, codec-export C5's fix pass), each
      figure positive with a source, 4K above 1080p
  R1  physical 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 GiB: budget = physical / 4, and per key at
      1080p and 4K the identical jobs admitted in sequence = max(1, ⌊budget / cost⌋), the
      cost the table's figure at the size
  R2  a writer row with no entry (a synthetic `unmeasured_webm` on `libvpx`, every real
      row being measured) costs the whole budget: it is admitted alone, then neither another
      of it nor an av1 job; an av1 job's booking keeps it out
  R3  an AVFoundation row (`h264`): no key, cost 0, `begin` books nothing, admitted beside a
      full ledger
  E1  `estimatedSeconds` per key at 1280×720, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3840×2160, 7680×4320
      and 150 / 300 / 1800 frames, and `sheetLine` its text
  E2  `estimateText` at 0.4, 2.4, 7.4, 57.4, 59.9, 60, 89, 90, 3569, 3570, 3600, 5399, 5400
  E3  `sheetLine` and `estimatedSeconds` nil for h264, and for `av1` at a rate that cannot
      be stepped (fps 0/1: no frame count, so no estimate rather than 0 frames)
  Q1  live, the shared queue and ledger, physical = 4 × the sheet job's cost: a headless
      Export… sheet writes W9 as `av1` Smaller; A (`av1`, A1), B and C (`h264`, A1) are
      enqueued. A waits with the exact sentence while the sheet runs; B then C run and
      complete before the sheet finishes; A launches only after the sheet's finish and
      completes; every file exists
  Q2  `AgentExports.track(A)` while held: status queued, `waiting` the sentence,
      `estimated_seconds` the table's
  Q3  physical 1 TiB, a sheet writing W9 as `av1` Faster: A runs before the sheet finishes
  Q4  `ExportQueueRowView.status`: the sentence for held A, "Waiting" for C while B runs;
      `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)` ends with the whole sentence for A (the status
      label truncates its tail) and has no "Waiting for memory" line for C
  Q5  the ledger is empty after Q1 drains, after Q3, after two `av1` jobs back to back (the
      second launched inside the first's `end`), after the queue refuses an empty
      project's `av1` job synchronously, and after a sheet does
App rows (`--app`, `RC_PROOF_APP`; instances in `tools/proof/work/encoder-limit/`):
  S1  File ▸ Export… on A1's project with `{"preset_id":"av1","encoder_speed":"smaller"}`
      pinned (`av1_export_proof.sheet_reading`'s pins): the summary label's second line is
      the table's "Estimated time: …"
  S2  the same with `{"preset_id":"h264"}`: no "Estimated" anywhere on the sheet
  X1  `export` av1 of A1, then `export_status` at once: `estimated_seconds` the table's; an
      h264 export's answer has none
  Z1  no instance log carries a `Frame Job: ` line

  python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py [--probe] [--app debug|release|<.app>]
                                             [--mutant NAME]

`--probe` runs B0–Q5 alone. `--mutant NAME` builds the probe over a copy of `app/Sources`
with the mutant's anchor replaced and runs the probe rows: exit 1 when every row it names
    if binary is None:
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, why)
        return None
    answer_path, out = folder / "answer.json", folder / "out"
    answer_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(av1.AV), str(out), str(answer_path)], 1500,
                      cwd=str(folder))
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer_path.exists():
        why = "the probe did not run: " + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-400:]
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, why)
        return None
    answer = json.loads(answer_path.read_text())
    check("B0", True, f"built and answered ({folder})")
    score_probe(answer)
    return answer


def score_probe(answer):
    tables = Tables(answer)
    # P0
    want = set(KEYS.values())
    problems = []
    for label, table in (("memory", tables.memory), ("time", tables.time)):
        if set(table) != want:
            problems.append(f"{label} keys {sorted(map(str, table))}")
    for key, figure in tables.memory.items():
        if not (0 < figure["at1080"] < figure["at2160"]) or not figure["source"]:
            problems.append(f"memory {key} {figure}")
    for key, entry in tables.time.items():
        f = entry["perFrame"]
        if not (0 < f["at1080"] < f["at2160"]) or "provisional" not in f["source"]:
            problems.append(f"time {key} {f}")
    check("P0", not problems, f"{len(tables.memory)} memory and {len(tables.time)} time "
          f"entries; {problems or 'all positive, 4K above 1080p, sourced'}")

    # R1
    misses, seen = [], set()
    for row in answer["r1"]:
        budget = row["physicalGiB"] * GIB // 4
        cost = tables.cost(row["key"], row["width"] * row["height"], budget)
        admitted = max(1, budget // cost) if cost else None
        seen.add((row["physicalGiB"], row["key"], row["width"]))
        if (row["budget"], row["cost"], row["admitted"]) != (budget, cost, admitted):
            misses.append(f"{row['physicalGiB']} GiB {row['key']} {row['width']}: "
                          f"{(row['budget'], row['cost'], row['admitted'])} ≠ "
                          f"{(budget, cost, admitted)}")
    full = len(seen) == len(PHYSICAL) * len(KEYS) * len(SIZES_R)
    sample = [r for r in answer["r1"] if r["physicalGiB"] == 32 and r["width"] == 3840]
    check("R1", full and not misses,
          f"{len(answer['r1'])} cases; misses {misses[:4]}; at 32 GiB and 4K "
          + ", ".join(f"{r['key']} {r['admitted']}" for r in sample))

    # R2
    r2 = answer["r2"]

    for label, table in (("memory", tables.memory), ("time", tables.time)):
        if set(table) != want:

    for key, figure in tables.memory.items():
        if not (0 < figure["at1080"] < figure["at2160"]) or not figure["source"]:
            problems.append(f"memory {key} {figure}")
    for key, entry in tables.time.items():
        f = entry["perFrame"]

| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the picture. | Off |

Under the controls, a readout line describes the file and a footnote names the codec, the container and the rates the file will use. Every number they show is the size, rate and duration the file will actually have.

- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`. For **AV1 (MP4)**, **AV1 (WebM)**, **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** a second line estimates how long the export will take: `Estimated time: about 25 s` (in 5-second steps under a minute, then minutes, then hours and minutes). It follows the format, Speed, size and range, and it is only an estimate: the figures behind it come from one measured export per format, so a busy Mac or a heavy timeline takes longer. The other formats show no estimate.
- **Footnote:** the codec, the container (left out when it is the same word, as in `GIF`), the AV1 speed (`AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`; VP9 has none: `VP9 · WEBM`, `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`), the video rate, the audio rate (`192 kbps audio`), the loudness target (`−14 LUFS`) and `alpha` when the format keeps transparency. When you pick a Quality tier and the format sets its own rate, it reads `format's own rate` instead of a number.


The **Speed** row sits under Format (under Dynamic Range in an HDR project). It is live only on **AV1 (MP4)** and **AV1 (WebM)**; on every other format it is greyed out and keeps your last choice. **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** have one speed, so the row is greyed out there too.

| Choice | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Faster** | The quickest AV1 export, a slightly larger file for the same picture. |
| **Balanced** | The default. |
| **Smaller file** | The slowest AV1 export, the smallest file for the same picture. |

AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, so they take longer than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder. The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in presets.

**Window ▸ Export Queue** lists queued exports. It opens on its own whenever you click **Add to Queue**.

- Jobs run **one at a time**, in the order they were added, while you keep editing.
- An **AV1** or **VP9** job also waits for memory. These formats are encoded in software and use a lot of it: about 1.2–2.3 GB at 1080p and 4.4–7.9 GB at 4K for AV1, depending on Speed, and about 0.4–0.5 GB at 1080p and 1.1–1.6 GB at 4K for VP9. All AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job at once, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may use up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. A queued AV1 or VP9 job that would go over waits until enough of them finish, and its row says why. The row's status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit, which at most window widths is before the figures; hold the pointer over the row and its tooltip ends with the whole sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB." While it waits, a later job that fits runs first. When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large. An **Export…** sheet never waits: it is counted, and starts straight away.
- A job holds the timeline **as it was when you confirmed it**, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics. Edits, undos, relinks and even closing the document afterwards do not change what it writes.
- Each row shows the file's name and its state: **Waiting** (or the memory wait above), *Writing · 42 %* (or the measuring phase), the "Exported …" line with its loudness figures, **Cancelled.**, **Cancelled before it started.**, or the reason a job failed. The tooltip shows the full path, the format, size and frame rate, the whole memory-wait sentence while a job waits for memory, and any graphic warnings.
- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
- Captions are burned in, never a switchable subtitle track.
- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
- The estimated time comes from one measured export per format on one Mac, and is provisional until it is measured on a quiet machine.
- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

# Objections

## 1
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** Step 7 rewrites the shared `run` prefix to the C6b string ("GH5 borough market 4K 25p, median of three runs per key and size, C6b"). Every memory figure is built as `run + "<key>; load …"`, so each memory figure that keeps its C6a value would then name C6b's run and fixture. That covers `av1_webm:faster` and `av1_webm:smaller`, which C6b does not run under the 10 % rule, and any key where step 5's max rule picks the C6a figure. Those sources would be false, against the rule that every constant names its source.
- **Evidence:** `app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift:74-76` (one `run` string), `:93-101` (the `av1_webm:faster`/`:smaller` memory sources are `run + …`), and spec lines 79 ("Keys C6b did not run keep theirs", "The source names whichever wins") against line 83 (`run` becomes the C6b string).
- **Suggested change:** Keep C6a's current `run` text as its own constant (for example `c6aRun`, as `alphaRun` already is) for every memory figure C6a still wins, and use the new C6b `run` only for figures C6b measured.

## 2
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** `written_frames` is computed from the `done` answer's `duration` and `fps`, and those are the resolved export *settings*, not anything read from the file. So the "more than 1 frame off is the row's `error`" check only catches a range that resolved wrong. A 4K row that drops or duplicates frames would pass, which defeats step 4's "writes the wrong frame count is a finding" on exactly the new 4K rows.
- **Evidence:** `app/Sources/AgentServer+ExportResult.swift:25-27` (`"fps": settings.fps…`, `"duration": settings.duration`), returned as the `done` status by `AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift` `status(_:)`. Spec line 32 derives `written_frames` from those fields, and line 36 deletes `out.*` before anything reads the file.
- **Suggested change:** Count the frames actually in `out.*` (for example `ffprobe -count_frames`/`-count_packets`, as the proofs already need ffmpeg) before deleting it, and compare that count to `expected_frames`.

## 3
- **Risk category:** missing-edge-case
- **Claim:** Step 1's check runs `--derive` over `2026-10-28/memory.json` given as both arguments, and expects exit 2 for "same frame count". That file's rows predate C6b: they have `frames`/`written_frames` but no `expected_frames`, `run` or `seconds_range`. A `--derive` that reads the new row keys would crash with a KeyError traceback instead of exiting 2. Also, the file holds only C5's fix-pass rows (4 rows: `vp9_alpha_webm`, `vp9_webm:sdr`), not C6a's run.
- **Evidence:** Running `json.load` on `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/2026-10-28/memory.json` in the worktree gives 4 rows whose keys are `key, preset, encoder_speed, hlg, width, height, frames, load_1min, …, written_frames, per_frame_seconds, log_complaints`, with no `expected_frames`. The file is rewritten as `memory.json` by every default-label run (`encoder_memory_measure.py`, `main`).
- **Suggested change:** Specify that `--derive` reads `expected_frames` and falls back to `frames` on pre-C6b rows, and describe the file as the C5 fix-pass JSON.

verdict: revise
